answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a comet, before it can post or attest. A single bridge checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 227 aliases as a result costs 161 bonds held for 11 days each, plus the river attestations those aliases can never earn. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
